intro: An AI assistant for property managers on Mac is a voice helper that can see the screen you are working on. Lazur is one option: hold a key, ask a question, and it answers out loud in Outlook, Excel, AppFolio or any other app you have open. This guide covers where the workday goes, what to ask, and where to be careful with tenant data.
tldr: A property manager's day runs through records, fees, budgets, email and vendor work, according to the BLS duty list.
No source on this page measures how that time splits across computer tasks, so treat the numbers as context.
Lazur sees your screen only while you hold ⌥ ⌘, answers out loud, and types drafts you check before sending.
Keep tenant personal data out of AI tools unless your employer's policy allows it.

blocks.text: How property managers spend the workday

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics lists the core duties for this job. They include keeping rental and owner-request records, paying bills or handing the payments to someone else, collecting monthly fees, and preparing budgets and financial reports. Onsite managers also keep income and expense records up to date and submit regular expense reports. Almost every one of those tasks ends up in a spreadsheet, an inbox, or a web portal.

Here is the catch. No source on this page measures how a property manager splits the day across computer tasks. The BLS page does not mention email or computer use at all. So any ranking of tasks is a reading of the duty list, not a measurement. Use it as a starting point, then check it against your own week.

The closest hard number comes from a 2018 survey by West Monroe. It asked 500 US managers how many hours a day they spend on admin tasks. It covers managers in general, not property managers. The answers are self-reported. More than half of the group put admin at 3 hours or more a day. Examples in the survey include answering email and submitting expense claims.

Email is the other big time sink, though the numbers are weaker here. A secondary article attributes to McKinsey the finding that knowledge workers spend 28% of their workweek managing email. The McKinsey original was not available for checking, so treat that figure as unconfirmed. It is not a property management number either. It still fits the admin survey, where answering email is one of the named examples.
The computer work behind the job

Most of the day runs across three kinds of screens. Spreadsheets hold the rent roll, the fee schedule and the budget. Mail holds tenant and vendor threads. A browser holds the property management system. AppFolio's help page for its investor portal says it supports Google Chrome (preferred), Mozilla Firefox, Safari and Microsoft Edge. That page covers the investor portal only, so check your own AppFolio setup too.

items: Excel or Google Sheets: rent rolls, fee schedules, owner budgets.
Outlook or Gmail: tenant threads, vendor quotes, owner questions.
A browser: AppFolio, vendor portals, and city or county websites.
Apple Calendar and Reminders: inspections, lease renewals, owner calls.

blocks.text: The BLS also notes that property managers often spend much of their time away from their desks. Lazur runs on the Mac, so it helps where that Mac is. If you spend the afternoon on site, you can still set a reminder by voice with the everyday commands. Sort the email back at the desk.
A realistic day and what you would say to Lazur

The day below is a realistic workday for an onsite or portfolio manager. Each line is something you could say out loud while you hold ⌥ ⌘. Lazur answers from what is on your screen, types text when you ask for it, and never clicks for you. The times are a guide, not a rule.
Tenant email: drafts, replies and dictation

Email is where tone matters most. A short reply to a leak report can calm a tenant or make things worse. Open the thread in Outlook for Mac, hold ⌥ ⌘, and ask Lazur to summarize what the tenant wants. Then ask for a draft in your own words. Lazur types it for you to paste or edit. You read it, change it and press Send yourself.

Microsoft's release notes list Outlook for Mac 16.114, dated October 14, 2026, and a later 16.114.3 build dated October 27, 2026. Check your version under Outlook > About Outlook before you follow a step that depends on a menu name. Gmail works the same way for drafting, since Lazur reads the screen either way.

For longer replies, hold fn and dictate. Lazur turns your speech into clean, formatted text and types it at the cursor in any app. You can add names to a personal dictionary, so property names and vendor names come out right the first time.

items: Leave the thread open in Outlook for Mac. Keep the lease notes in another window if you need them.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask: summarize this thread and say what the tenant is asking for.
Say the outcome you want. Include the date, the time window and the next step.
Read the draft out loud once. Change any promise you cannot keep, such as a repair date you do not control.
Click Reply yourself, check the recipients, and send.

blocks.title: Written notices carry legal weight
blocks.text: Notices and replies can become evidence. Keep the wording neutral and consistent across tenants. If a message touches a protected class, a disability, or a rule you are unsure about, check with your broker or counsel before you send. Lazur does not know your lease terms unless you tell it.
Rent rolls, fees and budgets in Excel or Google Sheets

A rent roll lists each unit, the tenant, the rent due, and what has been paid. Late fees, deposits and owner splits sit in other columns. The formulas that tie those columns together break easily. Before you change a formula, hold ⌥ ⌘ on the cell and ask Lazur what it does. Lazur explains it in plain language and points at the cells it uses.

Here is a worked example. You open a rent roll in Excel for Microsoft 365 on Mac. The total of past-due balances comes out low. Some of the amounts are text, not numbers, so SUM skips them without a warning. Ask Lazur why the total looks wrong. It points at the column, explains the text values, and guides you through converting them. The fix is quick. Finding it by eye is slow.

For a summary by property, a pivot table does the grouping for you. The step-by-step guide is at [how to make a pivot table in Excel](/how-to/make-a-pivot-table-in-excel). Ask Lazur to walk you through Insert > PivotTable. It waits for each click. In Google Sheets, the path is Insert > Pivot table.
Watch for these mistakes in rent rolls and budgets.

items: Numbers stored as text. Totals skip them, and nothing warns you.
Hard-coded dates in formulas, so next month's rent roll breaks.
Merged cells in the header row, which get in the way of filters and pivot tables.
A total row pasted into the data, so the sum counts itself.
Pasting from a PDF without checking the decimal places.

blocks.text: Vendors, work orders and the AppFolio screen

Work orders and vendor portals are where the clicks pile up. AppFolio runs in a browser on Mac, so every screen is a web page. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where the work order status is. Lazur draws a circle and a label around the control on your screen. You do the clicking.

Lazur does not click buttons, edit records or operate other apps for you. When you ask how to do something, it guides you one step at a time and waits for each click. That helps when a status change needs care, such as closing a work order after a repair you have not confirmed. Verify before you close anything.
Research and vendor quotes without the tab pileup

Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. You ask for it, Lazur works in the background, and it comes back with a summary and a report. Use it to compare a few plumbers, lock vendors or pest control companies. Ask for the source of each claim. Confirm licensing and insurance with the vendor and your state's public records yourself.
Tenant data, privacy and your employer's rules

Tenant files hold Social Security numbers, bank details, income records, and sometimes medical or disability information. Your employer decides what can go into an AI tool. Follow that policy first. Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and Lazur says they are not stored. Lazur also says its content is never used to train AI models.

A product promise does not replace your company's rules. Do not paste a full tenant file into any AI tool. Crop or hide the sensitive fields first, and keep the question narrow. This page makes no compliance claims for Lazur. Ask your employer whether a tool needs review before you use it at work.
Mistakes property managers make with AI tools

items: Sending a draft you did not read aloud. Tone slips most in the third paragraph.
Asking for a legal answer about a lease. Ask your broker or counsel instead.
Letting the assistant guess an amount or a date. Give those yourself.
Asking about a screen that has changed. Refresh the page, then hold ⌥ ⌘ again.
Using a personal account for company tenant data. Follow the account rules your employer set.

blocks.text: Setting it up on your Mac

items: Download Lazur from /download. It runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
Open the app. The free Pro trial starts the first time you open it, and no credit card is needed.
Approve the permissions Lazur asks for. If a prompt gets missed, check System Settings > Privacy & Security.
Test it with one question. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where the export or print button is on the page you have open.
Hold fn and dictate one short owner note. Add property and vendor names to the personal dictionary.

blocks.text: Is it worth it for a small portfolio?

Portfolio growth is the plan for many firms. Buildium's 2025 industry report says 91% of companies plan to expand their portfolios in the next 2 years. Portfolio growth is their top priority for the seventh year in a row. More units usually means more of the same email and records. The BLS projects 4% employment growth for the occupation from 2025 to 2035.

BLS puts median pay at $69,990 a year, or $33.65 an hour. At that rate, an hour spent on records has a real cost. Count the hours you spend on email and records for one week. Then decide which tasks an assistant should take first. Current plans are on the [pricing page](/pricing).

faq.question: What is an AI assistant for property managers?
faq.answer: It is a voice helper that sees the screen you are working on and answers questions about it. Lazur is one example on Mac. It can read a screen, point at buttons, draft text, and set reminders. It does not run your property management system for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with AppFolio or Buildium?
faq.answer: Lazur works with any app that is open on screen, including browser-based systems such as AppFolio. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. Buildium's Mac support was not confirmed for this page, so check Buildium's help center.

faq.question: Does Lazur run on Windows?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is for macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: Can an AI assistant read tenant data?
faq.answer: It can see what is on screen while you hold the shortcut. Follow your company's policy on tenant data first. Do not paste full tenant files, bank details or medical notes into any AI tool unless your employer allows it.

faq.question: How much time do property managers spend on admin?
faq.answer: A 2018 West Monroe survey of 500 US managers found that 36% spend 3 to 4 hours a day on admin tasks and 23% spend 5 or more hours. It covers managers in general, and the answers are self-reported.

faq.question: Will Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at things and guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click. You do the clicking, the sending and the saving.

faq.question: Which version of Outlook for Mac do I need?
faq.answer: Microsoft's release notes list Outlook for Mac 16.114 from October 14, 2026, and 16.114.3 from October 27, 2026. Check your version under Outlook > About Outlook.

faq.question: What does Lazur cost?
faq.answer: See the pricing page for current plans. A free Pro trial starts the first time you open the app, and no credit card is needed.
